samples.summary: Substantial scope creep past the task's stated "pure wiring" boundary
samples.evidence: The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:3-5) states: "This task is pure wiring: no new document behaviour, no new file formats, no new model fields." The diff goes well beyond wiring: a whole new URL gate in `serialize/markdown.ts` (`isLiteralDestination`, `URI_CHARS`, `ENTITY_REFERENCE`, `HAS_SCHEME`, `SCHEME_RELATIVE`, `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI`, line-separator folding, alt escaping) that changes the output of the already-shipped `wafflebase docs content --format md` command; a rewrite of `resolvePageSetup` into a sanitisation boundary; a new throwing `assertUsablePageSetup` on a public engine API; `.docx` sectPr length sanitisation; and re-routing both exporters through the resolver. These are documented as review-round follow-ups and the docs (cli.md §6.5, docs-pagination.md) were updated, so the cost is contained — but the change now bundles engine hardening with a UI-surfacing task, making it hard to revert either half independently.

samples.summary: `getStore()` now returns a Proxy that guards one method while explicitly disclaiming being a boundary — heavy indirection for a wiring task
samples.evidence: `pageSetupGuardedStore` wraps the real `DocStore` in a `Proxy` with a memoized bound-member cache and a `set` trap, purely to intercept `setPageSetup`; its own comment concedes it "is NOT an access-control boundary" and that ~30 other mutators plus `getDoc()` forward untouched (#989). Every existing consumer of `getStore()` (docs-export-button.tsx:53, docs-find-bar.tsx:56, harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:470) now receives a proxied object with rebound methods. The stated goal — "one write path" for page setup — is already achieved by `writePageSetup` + `EditorAPI.setPageSetup`; the proxy is defence-in-depth over a single method at the cost of changing the identity/semantics of a widely-held public handle.

samples.summary: The page-setup floor is implemented twice (engine assert + React form), a duplication that has already diverged once
samples.evidence: `assertUsablePageSetup` (editor.ts) and the dialog's `error` computation are two independent implementations of the same rule (finite/non-negative margins, effective-box rotation, `MIN_CONTENT_PX` floor). The task doc's fourth round records that these two already drifted apart and produced an uncaught `RangeError` out of a React handler. Sharing only the constant, rather than exporting a predicate (e.g. `validatePageSetup(setup): string | null`) from `@wafflebase/docs`, leaves the same divergence available the next time either side changes — the repo's stated preference is reuse of shared logic rather than parallel copies.
searchedFor: grep for validatePageSetup / assertUsablePageSetup exports in packages/docs/src/index.ts

samples.summary: Keyboard format-painter behaviour changed, against the plan's explicit "shortcuts must keep behaving exactly as they do now"
samples.evidence: Plan step 2 (task doc:29-34) requires the `Mod+Shift+C` / `Mod+Alt+V` cases to be lifted unchanged. The lift also changes capture semantics: `captureFormatAtCursor` now takes a `formatSourcePosition()` (first *selected* character, block-walk fallback, table-rectangle first cell) instead of the caret, and drops `image`, `pageNumber` and `href` from the buffer. Both are defensible improvements, but they alter what the existing keyboard shortcut copies — behaviour change smuggled in under a criterion that asked for none.

samples.summary: Engine-level Markdown URL gate is documented only in the CLI design doc, not in a docs-package design doc, although the frontend download now depends on it
samples.evidence: The new emit rule lives in `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts` and is now consumed by two surfaces: the CLI and the new frontend Markdown download (`text-actions.ts`). It is described only in `docs/design/cli.md` §6.5 (a CLI-command doc). `docs-pdf-export.md`, which this change extended to cover the Markdown/plain-text export entries, says nothing about the gate, and no doc under `docs/design/docs/` records the serializer's URL contract — so the canonical subsystem doc for the docs engine does not state a rule its output now depends on.

samples.summary: DOCX importer's new page-setup sanitisation is not reflected in the DOCX import/export design doc
samples.evidence: `parsePageSetup` now drops non-finite/zero/negative `<w:pgSz>` and negative `<w:pgMar>` values in favour of defaults and routes the result through `resolvePageSetup` (clamping margins that exceed the page). The doc's "Page Setup (`<w:sectPr>`)" mapping table still describes a plain twips→px mapping with no mention of validation or fallback, so the canonical import doc no longer describes what the importer does.

samples.summary: `supportsPainter` duck-types an in-repo interface at runtime
samples.evidence: `supportsPainter()` probes `typeof editor.hasCopiedFormat === 'function'` to defend against an `EditorAPI` "a version behind". `EditorAPI` is defined in this monorepo and consumed by this package; the risk it guards against is a frontend type-checking gap, not a real versioning boundary. It adds a permanently-disabled UI state that no shipped configuration can reach.

samples.summary: Task doc names a `NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` constant that does not exist in the code
samples.evidence: The follow-up entry says "`NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS` in `text-editor.ts` strips them", but the implementation strips `image`/`pageNumber`/`href` by destructuring inside `captureFormatAtCursor`; grep finds the identifier only in this task file.
searchedFor: grep NON_PAINTABLE_INLINE_KEYS across repo (only the task doc matches)

samples.summary: Frontend Markdown export silently diverges from the CLI default (`inlineImages: true`) with no design-doc record
samples.evidence: `exportMarkdownAndDownload` passes `inlineImages: true` while `docs content --format md` defaults to false; the divergence is explained only in a code comment. `docs-pdf-export.md`'s new export-menu section does not mention it, so the two surfaces of the same serializer produce different files with no documented rule.
searchedFor: grep inline-images / inlineImages in docs/design/cli.md and docs/design/docs/docs-pdf-export.md
